text: $\mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{g})}⇌\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\frac{\mathrm{C}}{2}(\mathrm{g})$ The correct relationship between $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}},α$ and equilibrium pressure $\mathrm{P}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Starting from 1 mol of A with degree of dissociation $α$:

$\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g})⇌\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$

At equilibrium the moles are A $=1-α$, B $=α$, C $=\dfrac{α}{2}$, so the total is $1+\dfrac{α}{2}=\dfrac{2+α}{2}$.

Partial pressure = mole fraction $\times$ total pressure $P$:

$p_{\mathrm{A}}=\dfrac{2(1-α)P}{2+α},p_{\mathrm{B}}=\dfrac{2αP}{2+α},p_{\mathrm{C}}=\dfrac{αP}{2+α}$

$K_{P}=\dfrac{p_{\mathrm{B}}\quad p_{\mathrm{C}}^{1/2}}{p_{\mathrm{A}}}=\dfrac{2αP/(2+α)}{2(1-α)P/(2+α)}\times \left (\dfrac{αP}{2+α}\right )^{1/2}=\dfrac{α}{1-α}\times \dfrac{α^{1/2}P^{1/2}}{(2+α)^{1/2}}$

The factor 2 cancels between $p_{\mathrm{B}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{A}}$, so no $\sqrt{2}$ remains:

$K_{P}=\dfrac{α^{3/2}P^{1/2}}{(2+α)^{1/2}(1-α)}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Which of the following is least ionic?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By Fajans' rules, the covalent character of a chloride increases with the polarising power of its cation.

$\mathrm{K}{}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{Ba}{}^{2+}$ are large cations with noble-gas configurations and low polarising power, so $\mathrm{KCl}$ and $\mathrm{BaCl}{}_{2}$ are highly ionic.

$\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}$ has a pseudo-noble-gas configuration ($4d^{10}$); its d electrons shield the nucleus poorly, so it polarises the large $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ ion strongly and $\mathrm{AgCl}$ has the greatest covalent character of the four, which also explains why $\mathrm{AgCl}$ is insoluble in water while $\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{2}$ dissolves readily.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: The four quantum numbers for the electron in the outermost orbital of potassium (atomic no. 19) are
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The four quantum numbers for the outermost electron of potassium can be determined by first understanding the electronic configuration of potassium (atomic number 19). The electron configuration is as follows:

$1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}4s^{1}$

The outermost electron resides in the 4s orbital. 

The four quantum numbers are as follows:

Principal quantum number ($n$): This indicates the energy level or shell number of the electron and for the 4s orbital, $n=4$.

Azimuthal quantum number ($l$): This indicates the subshell or shape of the orbital. For an $s$ orbital, $l=0$.

Magnetic quantum number ($m$): This indicates the orientation of the orbital in space. Since there is only one orientation for $s$ orbitals, $m=0$.

Spin quantum number ($s$): This can be either $+\frac{1}{2}$ or $-\frac{1}{2}$. Typically, the first electron in an orbital has a spin of $+\frac{1}{2}$.

Thus, the four quantum numbers for the outermost electron of potassium are:

$n=4,l=0,m=0,s=+\frac{1}{2}$

This matches with Option B:

$\mathrm{n}=4,l=0,\mathrm{m}=0,s=+\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
Match List I with List II

  
    
    List - I
(Complex ion)
    
    List - II
(Electronic Configuration)
  

  
    (A)
    $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$
    (I)
    $t_{2g}{}^{2}e_{g}^{0}$

  
  
    (B)
    $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$
    (II)
    $t_{2g}{}^{3}e_{g}{}^{0}$
  
  
    (C)
    $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$
    (III)
    $t_{2g}{}^{3}e_{g}{}^{2}$
  
  
    (D)
    $[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$
    (IV)
    $t_{2g}{}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an octahedral field the d electrons enter $t_{2g}$ first; $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is a weak-field ligand ($\Delta _{o}$ smaller than the pairing energy), so beyond three electrons the $e_{g}$ orbitals fill before $t_{2g}$ pairs.

$[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{3}$, giving $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{0}$ (II).

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$; the high-spin arrangement is $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ (III).

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$, giving $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$ (IV).

$[\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$: $\mathrm{V}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{2}$, giving $t_{2g}^{2}e_{g}^{0}$ (I).

The matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Aniline reacts with con. $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$, followed by heating at $453-473\mathrm{K}$ gives $\mathrm{p}$-aminobenzene sulphonic acid, which gives blood red colour in the 'Lassaigne's test'.

Statement II : In Friedel - Craft's alkylation and acylation reactions, aniline forms salt with the $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$ catalyst. Due to this, nitrogen of aniline aquires a positive charge and acts as deactivating group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are true

Statement I is false but statement II is true

solution.body:
Statement I: Aniline with conc. $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ forms anilinium hydrogensulphate, which on heating at 453–473 K gives p-aminobenzenesulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid). It contains both N and S, so on fusion with sodium it forms $\mathrm{NaSCN}$, which gives blood-red $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]{}^{2+}$ with $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ in Lassaigne's test. Statement I is true.


[IMG]

Statement II: Aniline is a Lewis base and forms a salt with the Lewis acid $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$; the nitrogen then carries a positive charge and acts as a strongly deactivating group, so aniline does not undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation or acylation. Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
A sample of $\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{MgCO}_{3}$ weighed $2.21\mathrm{g}$ is ignited to constant weight of $1.152\mathrm{g}$. The composition of mixture is :

(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}:100,\mathrm{MgCO}_{3}:84$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the mixture contain $x$ g of $\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}$ and $(2.21-x)$ g of $\mathrm{MgCO}{}_{3}$. On ignition to constant weight both carbonates leave their oxides:

$\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CaO}+\mathrm{CO}{}_{2},\mathrm{MgCO}{}_{3}\longrightarrow \mathrm{MgO}+\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$

One mole of each carbonate gives one mole of oxide, so the residue is

$\dfrac{x}{100}\times 56+\dfrac{2.21-x}{84}\times 40=1.152$

$0.56x+0.4762(2.21-x)=1.152\Rightarrow 0.0838x=0.0996\Rightarrow x\approx 1.19\text{g}$

So the mixture is about $1.19$ g of $\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}$ and $1.02$ g of $\mathrm{MgCO}{}_{3}$; the small difference from $1.187$ g and $1.023$ g comes only from rounding of the residue mass.

Check with $1.187$ g $\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}$ and $1.023$ g $\mathrm{MgCO}{}_{3}$ (total $2.21$ g): $\mathrm{CaO}=1.187\times 0.56=0.665$ g and $\mathrm{MgO}=1.023\times \dfrac{40}{84}=0.487$ g, total $1.152$ g, matching the residue.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: From the vitamins $\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}_{1},\mathrm{B}_{6},\mathrm{B}_{12},\mathrm{C},\mathrm{D},\mathrm{E}$ and $\mathrm{K}$, the number of vitamins that can be stored in our body is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K are retained in the liver and in adipose (fat-depositing) tissue.

Water-soluble vitamins (the B group and C) are readily excreted in urine, so they cannot be retained in the body and must be supplied regularly in the diet; the one exception is vitamin $\mathrm{B}_{12}$, which is retained in the liver.

Of the vitamins given, those the body can retain are A, D, E, K and $\mathrm{B}_{12}$; $\mathrm{B}_{1}$, $\mathrm{B}_{6}$ and C cannot.

Hence, the answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
A diatomic molecule has a dipole moment of $1.2\mathrm{D}$. If the bond distance is $1\mathrm{A}^{\circ }$, then fractional charge on each atom is $_________$ $\times 10^{-1}$ esu.

(Given $1\mathrm{D}=10^{-18}$ esucm)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the fractional charge on each atom in a diatomic molecule, we can use the relationship between dipole moment (μ), charge (q), and distance (d):

$μ=q\times d$

Where:

μ is the dipole moment.

q is the magnitude of the charge on each atom.

d is the distance between the charges.

First, convert units to be consistent with esu:

Bond distance in cm: $1\mathrm{A}^{\circ }=1\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{cm}$

Dipole moment in esu·cm: $1.2\mathrm{D}=1.2\times 10^{-18}\mathrm{esucm}$

We are given that the bond distance ($d$) is $1\mathrm{A}^{\circ }$ and that the dipole moment $(μ$) is $1.2\mathrm{D}$. Using these values, we can calculate the charge ($q$) as follows:

$q=\frac{μ}{d}$

Now plug in the given values:

$q=\frac{1.2\times 10^{-18}\mathrm{esucm}}{1\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{cm}}$

$q=1.2\times 10^{-10}\mathrm{esu}$

$q=1.2\times 10^{-9}\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{esu}$

$q=0.0000000012\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{esu}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
The values of conductivity of some materials at $298.15\mathrm{K}\text{in}\mathrm{Sm}^{-1}$ are $2.1\times 10^{3}$,

 $1.0\times 10^{-16},1.2\times 10,3.91,1.5\times 10^{-2},1\times 10^{-7},1.0\times 10^{3}$.

 The number of conductors among the materials is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given conductivities at $298.15\text{K}$ are those of standard materials.

$2.1\times 10^{3}\text{S m}^{-1}$ (sodium), $1.0\times 10^{3}\text{S m}^{-1}$ (iron) and $1.2\times 10\text{S m}^{-1}$ (graphite) are electronic conductors, and $3.91\text{S m}^{-1}$ ($0.1\text{M}$ HCl) is an electrolytic conductor.

$1.5\times 10^{-2}\text{S m}^{-1}$ (silicon) and $1\times 10^{-7}\text{S m}^{-1}$ (copper(II) oxide) are semiconductors, and $1.0\times 10^{-16}\text{S m}^{-1}$ (glass) is an insulator.

Number of conductors $=3+1=4$.

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A compound $(x)$ with molar mass $108\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ undergoes acetylation to give product with molar mass $192\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. The number of amino groups in the compound $(x)$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acetylation replaces one H of each $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$ group by an acetyl group:

$\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}+\mathrm{HCl}$

Each acetylated amino group raises the molar mass by $43-1=42\text{g mol}^{-1}$ (gain of $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}$, loss of one H).

Total increase in molar mass $=192-108=84\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Number of amino groups $=\dfrac{84}{42}=2$, consistent with $x$ being a phenylenediamine, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}){}_{2}$ (molar mass $108\text{g mol}^{-1}$).

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
If 5 moles of an ideal gas expands from $10\mathrm{L}$ to a volume of $100\mathrm{L}$ at $300\mathrm{K}$ under isothermal and reversible condition then work, $\mathrm{w}$, is $-x\mathrm{J}$. The value of $x$ is $__________$.

(Given R = 8.314 J K${}^{-1}$ mol${}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
It is isothermal reversible expansion, so work done negative

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{W}=-2.303\mathrm{nRT}\log \left (\dfrac{\mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{V}_{1}}\right ) \\ =-2.303\times 5\times 8.314\times 300\log \left (\dfrac{100}{10}\right ) \\ =-28720.713\mathrm{J} \\ \equiv -28721\mathrm{J} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
The molarity of $1\mathrm{L}$ orthophosphoric acid $(\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4})$ having $70%$ purity by weight (specific gravity $1.54\mathrm{g}\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$) is $__________$ $\mathrm{M}$.

(Molar mass of $\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}=98\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Specific gravity (density) $=1.54\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cc}$.

Volume $=1\mathrm{L}=1000\mathrm{ml}$

Mass of solution $=1.54\times 1000$

$=1540\mathrm{g}$

$%$ purity of $\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}$ is $70%$

So weight of $\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}=0.7\times 1540=1078\mathrm{g}$

Mole of $\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{PO}_{4}=\frac{1078}{98}=11$

Molarity $=\frac{11}{1\mathrm{L}}=11$

text: $\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]$ for a reaction, $50%$ of $\mathrm{A}$ is decomposed in 120 minutes. The time taken for $90%$ decomposition of $\mathrm{A}$ is $_________$ minutes.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]$

So, order of reaction $=1$

$\mathrm{t}_{1/2}=120\min$

For $90%$ completion of reaction

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=\dfrac{2.303}{\mathrm{t}}\log \left (\dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}}\right ) \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{0.693}{\mathrm{t}_{1/2}}=\dfrac{2.303}{\mathrm{t}}\log \dfrac{100}{10} \\ \therefore \mathrm{t}=399\min . \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift
